newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER DESPITE LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES FIRMER DESPITE LIQUIDITY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mostly firmer on Tuesday despite a surplus of cash in the system, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank auctioned treasury bills worth Z$260 million at a yield of 16.52 percent, up from 16.49 on Monday and discount houses were selling the paper at 16.25 percent in the secondary market.
Dealers say they expect the money rates to strengthen in line with annual inflation which went up to 19.9 percent in March from 19 percent the previous month.

Bills maturing after 50, 60 and 90 days were on Tuesday being bought and sold at 17 and 16.50 percent respectively from 17 percent and 16.85 percent. Bankers acceptances edged up to 16.75 percent (buying) from 16.50 and were being sold at 16.50 percent, up from 16.25.
Call money added 0.25 percentage points to 16.25 percent in a market which opened with a Z$260 million surplus from a previous shortage of Z$247 million.
